prose.text: **The order.** - Phase A: the formatter, the linter, the rig library cases, the `KR` rehearsals through the integration layer (which   builds the root binaries they spawn), and the workspace unit layer. - The round: entries 6–19, `round` and `live` entries ONLY (`inputs#I2` item 9). Its after-reads of state other actors   move are keyed to the round. - After the span: the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole integration layer and   the operator pass.

**What is not run, and why.** - No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10). - No `--e2e` layer: no MCP, contract or path surface is touched; the rig is test-only. - No release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it). - `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job: no dependency is added. - No product file changes, so no smoke beyond the operator pass's harness boot.

**Bounds.** Every test start runs under a test-owned home. Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the rehearsals wait on the rig's exit under its `--deadline`. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and config; `--deadline 300` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are the round entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.

**No remove-the-guard control** is planned: the chunk adds no product guard. The arm's `lost` and `unread` words are made to fail by the pure cases of step 3 (entry 3), which produce each word from synthetic attribute words before any graded use.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)). The `KR` summary keys the live entries assert are this chunk's own print site (step 4), so each word is read printed before any graded use, in block order: - entry 3 runs the pure cases of step 3, which produce `kept`, `lost`, `unread` and the three readings; - entry 4 runs the rehearsals of step 6, which print the arm's own keys (`arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control:   told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kr-reading: kept`) and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent.

`kr-reading` on a real CLI is the reading itself, asserted only by the round's reading entries 18–19 (`inputs#I2` item 4 names the predicate). Their must-pass and must-fail control was read at P5 (`p5-controls.md` of the take-up run): each entry's exact `run`, typed in a scratch clone over a synthetic ledger, passes on `kept` and fails on `lost` and on an absent summary, each reading its own version alone.

prose.text: **The order.** - Phase A: the formatter, the linter, the rig library cases, the `KR` rehearsals through the integration layer (which   builds the root binaries they spawn), and the workspace unit layer. - The round: entries 6–19, `round` and `live` entries ONLY (`inputs#I2` item 9). Its after-reads of state other actors   move are keyed to the round. - After the span: the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole integration layer and   the operator pass.

**What is not run, and why.** - No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10). - No `--e2e` layer: no MCP, contract or path surface is touched; the rig is test-only. - No release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it). - `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job: no dependency is added. - No product file changes, so no smoke beyond the operator pass's harness boot.

**Bounds.** Every test start runs under a test-owned home. Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the rehearsals wait on the rig's exit under its `--deadline`. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and config; `--deadline 300` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are the round entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.

**No remove-the-guard control** is planned: the chunk adds no product guard. The arm's `lost` and `unread` words are made to fail by the pure cases of step 3 (entry 3), which produce each word from synthetic attribute words before any graded use.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)). The `KR` summary keys the live entries assert are this chunk's own print site (step 4), so each word is read printed before any graded use, in block order: - entry 3 runs the pure cases of step 3, which produce `kept`, `lost`, `unread` and the three readings; - entry 4 runs the rehearsals of step 6, which print the arm's own keys (`arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control:   told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kr-reading: kept`) and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent.

`kr-reading` on a real CLI is the reading itself, asserted only by the round's reading entries 18–19 (`inputs#I2` item 4 names the predicate). Their must-pass and must-fail control was read at P5 (`p5-controls.md` of the take-up run): each entry's exact `run`, typed in a scratch clone over a synthetic ledger, passes on `kept` and fails on `lost` and on an absent summary, each reading its own version alone.
